news.headline: US Airstrikes on Iran's Larak Island — WTI Crude +5.9% Yesterday, Brent Near $95
news.what_happened: US forces struck Iranian rocket launcher positions on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on September 1, 2026, the latest in a series of US-Iran military exchanges ongoing since March 2026. Strait of Hormuz commercial traffic is down 90% from normal. WTI crude surged ~5.9% yesterday to $90.22 close, with Brent reaching ~$95/bbl. Crude is up 13% over the past month and 38% YoY.
news.why_it_matters: India imports ~85% of its crude oil, much of it from the Gulf. Sustained crude at $90-95 directly widens India's current account deficit, pressures the rupee, and fuels inflation. OMCs face margin squeeze if fuel prices aren't raised. Airlines bear massive fuel cost spikes. Upstream producers (ONGC, OIL) earn higher realization per barrel.

news.headline: US S&P 500 -0.71%, Nasdaq -1.03%; Nikkei -2.55%, KOSPI -3% — Global Risk-Off
news.what_happened: US equity markets sold off on September 1 as the US-Iran conflict reignited. Bond yields surged (US 10Y at 4.796%, up from 4.758%) reflecting inflation fears from oil prices. Asian markets extended the selloff overnight: Nikkei -2.55%, Hang Seng -0.93%, KOSPI -3% at open. GIFT Nifty indicates Indian market to open ~24,030, down ~145 points from the Nifty 50 previous close of 24,175.
news.why_it_matters: A broad global risk-off with rising bond yields is the worst combination for Indian equities. FIIs are likely to be net sellers. Rising US 10Y yields compress PE multiples and make EM assets less attractive. Indian banking, NBFCs, and real estate face double pressure from yield fears and FII outflows.

news.headline: India GDP Q1 FY27 at 7.8% — Manufacturing +9.2%, Private Investment +11.9%
news.what_happened: India's GDP grew 7.8% YoY in the April-June 2026 quarter, beating estimates. Manufacturing expanded 9.2% and fixed investment rose 11.9%, signalling the long-awaited private capex cycle is finally activating. GVA grew 8.2%.
news.why_it_matters: Strong domestic fundamentals provide a cushion. Capital goods, construction, and cement sectors benefit from the accelerating investment cycle. However, today's global risk-off is likely to dominate this positive signal. Medium-term outlook for domestic capex plays remains constructive.

news.headline: Natural Gas +1.83% — Energy Substitute Demand Spikes as Geopolitical Crisis Continues
news.what_happened: Natural Gas futures rose to $2.957/MMBtu (+1.83%) as energy markets price in substitution demand from disrupted oil flows. Fertilizer producers relying on gas feedstock face rising input costs.
news.why_it_matters: Higher gas prices squeeze fertilizer EBITDA margins directly. CGD players (IGL, MGL) face regulated pricing pressure if gas costs rise but tariff hikes are delayed by regulators. Coal may see incremental demand as an energy substitute.

picks.catalyst: Crude WTI at $90.93/bbl (+0.79%), Brent ~$95 — sustained by US-Iran Strait of Hormuz conflict
picks.logic: ONGC is India's largest upstream oil producer. Every $1 increase in crude oil price directly raises ONGC's net realization by ~₹2,500-3,000 Cr annually. With crude now at $90+ vs the FY27 budget assumption of ~$75/bbl, ONGC's earnings upside is substantial. Unlike OMCs, upstream producers do not face marketing margin compression — they benefit purely from higher realisation. Geopolitical escalation (US-Iran) indicates crude prices will remain elevated for the session.
